title: FICTIONAL: Randomized Phase 2 Study of ZX-4012 Plus Docetaxel Versus Docetaxel Alone in Previously Treated Advanced NSCLC
summary: This fictional study tests whether adding ZX-4012, a once-daily tablet, to standard docetaxel chemotherapy helps people with advanced non-small cell lung cancer whose cancer grew after platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy live longer without their cancer getting worse. Participants are randomly assigned to docetaxel with ZX-4012 or docetaxel alone and come to the clinic every three weeks for treatment, blood tests and scans.

rules.raw_text: Age >= 18 years at the time of signing informed consent.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), stage IIIB, IIIC or IV (AJCC 8th edition), not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy.

Radiographic disease progression on or after one prior platinum-based chemotherapy regimen and one prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody, given in combination or sequentially, for advanced or metastatic disease.

Radiographic disease progression on or after one prior platinum-based chemotherapy regimen and one prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody, given in combination or sequentially, for advanced or metastatic disease.
No more than 2 prior lines of systemic therapy for advanced or metastatic disease.
At least one measurable lesion according to RECIST version 1.1.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Absolute neutrophil count >= 1.5 x 10^9/L (1,500/mm3)
Hemoglobin >= 9.0 g/dL (90 g/L); transfusion is allowed if given at least 14 days before the first dose
Creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault)
AST and ALT <= 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN), or <= 5 x ULN for patients with liver metastases
rules.note: Liver-metastasis exception (<= 5 x ULN) is not representable; the base threshold is used.

rules.raw_text: Total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN
Able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.
Untreated or symptomatic central nervous system metastases. Patients with previously treated brain metastases are eligible if radiologically stable for at least 4 weeks and off corticosteroids.
Active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
History of interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids, or current pneumonitis.
Active infection requiring systemic therapy, including known uncontrolled HIV infection, active hepatitis B or hepatitis C.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
Unable to swallow oral medication.
rules.note: No vocabulary field for ability to swallow tablets; flagged, not guessed.
